title: Policy Authoring Workbench: Region & Fallback Simulation
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Add a Policy Authoring Workbench into the Console that lets customers author routing rules combining region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants, then validate and run traffic simulations with realistic latency/cost heuristics. The workbench is a lightweight, guided flow for PMs and platform engineers to preview how requests would be routed across regions, capacity tiers, and downgraded model variants during capacity constraints or degraded availability.
acceptance_criteria: Workbench UI allows composing rules by region (e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1), tier (hosted, dedicated, private), and model variant fallback chains

Preview simulator accepts a sample traffic profile (rps, geo distribution, latency targets) and produces a simulated routing outcome with per-route metrics (expected latency, cost delta, fallback events)
Inline validation surfaces conflicts (unreachable routes, circular fallbacks), and suggests fixes with one-click auto-corrections
Policy drafts can be saved as named revisions and diffed against live policies in the Console
Simulator output links to trace examples and explains how automatic fallback triggers (capacity, SLO breach, region outage) would re-route requests
qa_checks: validation logic unit tests cover 95% branches
end-to-end simulation with synthetic traffic in staging region
manual verification of UI diff and revert flows
notes: Motivation: customers are asking for a single place to reason about multi-region routing tradeoffs without running production experiments.
We should model three failure modes: capacity-exhaustion, increased median latency, region blackout. Each should map to a clear fallback action in the policy editor.
We will expose projected cost delta for enabling dedicated tiers vs staying on hosted for the simulated profile.
Keep the initial rule language declarative and compatible with planned routing engine (binds to runtime policy schema v2).
progress_updates: 2025-01-12 - Kickoff: aligned PM, design, and infra on scope. Agreed MVP excludes RBAC for drafts (future phase).
2025-01-20 - Design review: high-fidelity mockups approved with minor copy updates; added 'explain fallback' panel per row.
2025-01-28 - Engineering spike completed: simulator PoC returns simulated routing percentages and latency estimates using sampled historical telemetry.
2025-02-02 - Integration work: console front-end consumes /api/policy/simulate; backend needs throttling and cost estimator parity with billing service.
open_questions: Should the simulator allow stochastic failures (random region outages) or only deterministic scenarios?
What are guardrails for saving a draft that would route production traffic differently than the live policy? (require explanation or approval?)
Do we expose estimated token-level cost or a relative percentage for the simulation?
followups: Add audit log entry for policy simulate actions in the next sprint (security/observability ask)
Hook up canary rollout button from workbench to the existing rollout service once validation passes
Design microcopy for 'explain fallback' modal and place it behind an experiment flag for early testers
estimated_impact: Reduces time-to-ship routing rules by ~40% for teams managing multi-region deployments
Expected to lower customer outage-induced model downgrades by surfacing fallback gaps pre-deployment
